memories.author: D05
memories.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia, vitamin D deficiency, epilepsy. Symptoms: nocturia 2-3 times, mild fatigue, no recent seizures. Exam: prostate mildly enlarged, non-tender; neurologic normal. Spirometry not indicated.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS
finasteride 5 mg OD
cholecalciferol 60000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks
levetiracetam 500 mg BD
lamotrigine 50 mg BD

memories.author: D05
memories.text: EEG: background activity normal, no epileptiform discharges.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Ultrasound KUB: prostate volume 38 mL, post‑void residual 25 mL, no hydronephrosis.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Started tamsulosin, notice less urgency at night. Vitamin D capsules taken as directed. No seizure since last month.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia improved, vitamin D deficiency still low, epilepsy stable. Symptoms: nocturia once nightly, mild bone aches. Exam: prostate slightly smaller, no tenderness. Spirometry FEV1 2.8 L (92% pred), FVC 3.4 L, ratio 0.82, unchanged. ACT score 22 (well controlled). Technique checked: correct.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia stable, vitamin D deficiency now adequate, epilepsy unchanged. Symptoms: nocturia once, no bone pain. Exam: prostate 35 mL, PVR 20 mL. memories.author: D05
memories.text: Benign prostatic hyperplasia controlled, vitamin D sufficient, epilepsy seizure‑free for 8 months. Symptoms: nocturia once, no adverse drug effects. Exam: prostate 33 mL, PVR 18 mL. Spirometry FEV1 3.0 L (98% pred), FVC 3.6 L, ratio 0.83, +0.2 L from baseline. ACT 24 (well controlled). Technique checked: correct. Smoking status: never.
